title: The Mark That Stops Ships Sinking
coreQuestion: What is the mark painted on the side of a ship's hull?

facts.claim: Load lines are indicated by special markings on the hull.
Additional marks have been added over the years, allowing for different water densities and expected sea conditions.
This marking was invented in 1876 by Samuel Plimsoll.
It has long been recognized that limitations on the draught to which a ship may be loaded make a significant contribution to her safety.
Load lines set the minimum freeboard of a ship.

narration.text: Those painted marks on a ship's side are load lines.
The marking was invented in 1876 by Samuel Plimsoll.
Over the years, extra marks were added for different water densities.
They also allow for the sea conditions a ship expects to meet.
A few painted lines on the hull, each one for a different sea.

editorial.hook: Those painted marks on a ship's side are load lines.
editorial.openingLine: Those painted marks on a ship's side are load lines.
editorial.secondBeat: The marking was invented in 1876 by Samuel Plimsoll.
editorial.mechanism: Markings on the hull show how deep a ship may be loaded, with extra marks for different water densities and expected sea conditions
editorial.expectedConsequence: A ship is loaded to the line for the water and the sea it will meet
editorial.misconception: The marks look like a builder's decoration, but they are load lines.
editorial.payoff: A few painted lines on the hull, each one for a different sea.
